APPENDIX C
Method, sources & limitations

Stated plainly so any figure here can be audited or challenged.

Where the data comes from
  Source: Meta Marketing API v21.0, queried 08 September 2026 with an operator token carrying ads_read,
  ads_management, business_management and read_insights.
  Scope: 112 ad accounts, 74 Facebook Pages and 26 Business Managers visible to this token.
  Lifetime spend per account comes from the account's own amount_spent field, which is cumulative since the account
  opened — not from the insights window.

The 37-month boundary
Meta's Insights API refuses any query starting more than 37 months back. Month-level detail, impressions, clicks, reach,
placement, country and attributed results therefore cover 2023-08 to 2026-09 only. Lifetime spend totals are not limited
this way, so the career total is complete even where the monthly breakdown is not. Of $256,515 total, $249,241 (97.2%)
falls inside the detailed window and $7,274 predates it.

How industries were assigned
Many ad accounts carried several brands at once, so attribution is done per campaign, not per account. Each of the
campaigns with spend is matched against a brand dictionary built from the campaign names actually observed in these
accounts (bilingual English/Arabic). Where a campaign name carries no brand signal, its spend is split pro-rata across the
brands already identified inside that same account — and only when those identified campaigns represent at least 30% of
the account, so a small amount of evidence can never decide a large amount of spend. Where that test fails, the spend is
reported as unattributed rather than assigned. Every campaign and its attribution basis is listed in
data/11_campaigns.csv.

Currency conversion
Accounts bill in EGP, USD and QAR. Each month's spend is converted at that month's actual USD rate (monthly USD/EGP
and USD/KWD series; QAR is pegged at 3.64). Pre-window residual spend is converted at the average rate across the
account's pre-window life. Using today's rate instead would understate 2021–2022 work by roughly 3×.

Integrity check performed
For every account opened after the window start, the independent amount_spent field was compared against the sum of
monthly insights; all reconciled within 3%.

4 accounts were found where amount_spent under-reports actual spend — Meta resets that counter when a spend
cap changes. On one account it read 206 QAR against 148,719 QAR of observed delivery. Lifetime spend is therefore taken
as the greater of the reported field and the observed insights, which is why the totals here are higher than Ads Manager's
own lifetime column would suggest.

Finally, the campaign-level attribution is reconciled back to the account-level verified totals: the two agree to the dollar
($256,515).

Known limitations — stated deliberately
  2018–2021 work is not represented here. The earliest ad account dates to 2018-03-09, but no campaign records
  exist on it before 2022. Early-career freelance campaigns were run inside client-owned ad accounts that this token no
  longer has access to. That work is real but not machine-verifiable from this vantage point, so it is excluded rather than
  estimated.
  Non-Meta channels are absent. Google, TikTok, Snapchat and LinkedIn spend is not in this dataset — this is a Meta
  record only.

Reach is not additive across accounts; the same person may be counted in more than one account's unique reach.
   Attributed results follow Meta's attribution settings at the time each campaign ran, which changed across iOS 14.5 and
   subsequent attribution updates.
